sheet-1-1.description: The main map of sheet 1 shows Main Street in Cranbury south of Brainerd Lake, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with Station Road leaving it towards the east at the bottom of the sheet. Main Street runs down the left half of the sheet from the lake and the Waste Way at the top, where the Cranbury Feed Mill (water power) stands by the stream, to the junction with Station Road near the bottom edge. West of Main Street (block 25) are frame dwellings, a livery, a harness room, a motion picture house, sheds and, near the bottom, the First Presbyterian Church with its Sunday school rooms and three long hitching sheds. East of Main Street (block 26) are dwellings, wagon houses, storage sheds and the closed United States Hotel. Station Road runs from Main Street to the right edge of the sheet with dwellings, auto sheds, a blacksmith and wood working shop and the fire department house on its south side (block 27), and vacant fields beyond. Water pipes of 4 and 8 inches and hydrants are drawn along both streets. The upper right quarter of the sheet holds the key map of Cranbury, the title cartouche (August 1916, population 1,000), notes on water facilities and the fire department, and the index; a small inset at the left shows an ice house on Brainerd Lake. Neither is part of this map.
notes: Main is today South Main Street; Station Road keeps its name.

Placed from the single junction of Main Street and Station Road (anchored, scale set to 8.8 px per foot); the rotation measured from the street lines there (-42.8 degrees) differs by about 25 degrees from the sheet's north arrow and from sheets 2 and 3 (-18 degrees). With the compass rotation the top of Main Street would land about 115 m west of the modern street, so the measured rotation was kept. Low confidence.
The inset with the ice house on Brainerd Lake (block 26, no exposure any side) and the key map are not georeferenced.
Buildings of note: Cranbury Feed Mill, United States Hotel (closed), First Presbyterian Church and Sunday school rooms, fire department.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the business centre of Cranbury along Main Street between Park Place at the top and Brainerd Lake at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north slightly to the left of straight up. Main Street runs down the left third of the sheet; Scott Avenue crosses below the middle and Maplewood Avenue runs parallel to Main Street on the right. Park Place crosses the top, with the stub of Wesley Place above it. The west side of Main Street holds the J. S. Silvers and Bro. Co. wholesale grocers, drug, grocery and hardware stores with a tin shop, a bakery, a boarding house, the Schultz Memorial M. E. Church with its hitching shed, a printing office, billiards and a barber, and the public school at the left edge. On the east side are the bank, the post office with a lodge room above, the Cranbury Water Co. well, pump house and elevated tank, the fire department with its hook and ladder truck, a furniture and undertaker's shop and the public library, with dwellings, autos sheds, wagon houses and fowl houses behind. Maplewood Avenue has detached dwellings, and vacant fields lie beyond it. Brainerd Lake fills the lower right corner, with ice houses at its upper end. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along Main Street, Scott Avenue and Maplewood Avenue.
notes: Main is today North Main Street; Park Place is Park Place East and Park Place West.
Buildings of note: J. S. Silvers and Bro. Co. wholesale grocers, Schultz Memorial M. E. Church, public school, bank, post office, Cranbury Water Co., fire department, public library.
50 ft. Business centre: Main, Park Pl, Scott Av, Maplewood Av, Brainerd Lake.

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 shows Main Street in the north of Cranbury from Park Place at the bottom to the edge of the sheet, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north slightly to the left of straight up. Main Street runs down the left half of the sheet; Brainerd Place leaves it to the west and Westminster Place to the east, and Park Place crosses at the bottom. Wesley Place runs between Westminster Place and Park Place, and Maplewood Avenue runs diagonally up the right side. The blocks west of Main Street (17 and 19) are lined with frame dwellings on long lots, with a grocery and a wholesale grocery near Park Place. Between Main Street and Maplewood Avenue lies a large cemetery (block 18) with the Second Presbyterian Church and its Sunday school rooms at its lower corner and a drive along its edge. Block 20, between Westminster and Park Places, holds dwellings, a harness shop, a confectionery and meat shop, a sausage factory and repair shop and long hitching sheds; block 21 has dwellings and a warehouse with an auto shed. Maplewood Avenue carries a row of dwellings, and the Cranbury Feeble Minded Institute is named at the top margin. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along Main Street and Maplewood Avenue. The inset at the top centre is a separate part.
notes: Main is today North Main Street; Brainerd Place is today Bunker Hill Road; Park Place is Park Place East and Park Place West.
Buildings of note: Second Presbyterian Church and Sunday school rooms, cemetery, Cranbury Feeble Minded Institute (named at the top).

50 ft. Two parts: 1 main map, Main from Park Pl north (Brainerd Pl = Bunker Hill Rd, Westminster, Wesley, Maplewood, cemetery); 2 inset at top: Main at Princeton Road (Plainsboro Rd), Cranbury Garage.

sheet-3-2.description: The inset at the top of sheet 3 shows Main Street at its junction with Princeton Road, north of the main part of the sheet, drawn at the same 50 feet to an inch inside a heavy border. Main Street runs down the middle of the inset, 66 feet wide, and Princeton Road crosses its lower edge. West of Main Street (block 15) are two frame dwellings; east of it (block 16) are the Cranbury Garage, a concrete block building with room for 20 cars and a buried gasoline tank, a brick dwelling, another dwelling and auto sheds. The edges of the inset are marked no exposures.
notes: Main is today North Main Street; Princeton Road is today Plainsboro Road.
Placed from the single junction of Main Street and Princeton Road (anchored, scale from the main part, rotation from the measured street lines); low confidence.
